title: arxiv_2602.10784v2
universal_lens: A statistical fusion of supervised and unsupervised learning for real-time defensive scheme prediction in American football via player trajectory and hidden Markov modeling. Hierarchical Bayesian Markov models enable structured inference across spatial-temporal sports data through shared random effects and identifiable transition dynamics.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of defensive coverage using incremental feature sets from pre-snap motion and HMM-derived latent states, enabling probabilistic coverage classification with conformal uncertainty quantification. GSI leverages conformal predictive distributions over latent states to quantify uncertainty in defender-offensive player assignments via hierarchical HMMs.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine mapping pre-snap motion to latent defensive assignments via state-transition dynamics of player trajectories, supporting real-time coverage scheme forecasting. GSE employs state-transition kernels derived from observed trajectories to simulate tactical positioning and predict defensive behavior under varying game contexts.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to decode guarding assignments in football plays. The core challenge is translating noisy, multidimensional player trajectory data into accurate latent state sequences representing coverage relationships. HMMs excel because they naturally incorporate temporal persistence, penalizing spurious state switches driven by measurement error. By contrast, standard k-means clustering treats each frame independently, leading to highly variable and unreliable assignments when players occupy similar horizontal zones. The authors demonstrate this via Figure 4, showing that HMM maintains consistent coverage on Mecole Hardman even when he crosses paths with the running back. Crucially, the transition probability matrices in Table 2 reveal that most defenders rarely switch assignments, indicating strong persistence. However, elevated probabilities exist for similar horizontal zones, suggesting occasional misassignment risk. The cross-fitting procedure in Figure 5 compares HMM-derived features against elastic net and XGBoost classifiers, showing that HMM features improve predictive performance across all metrics. This work establishes a rigorous mathematical framework for extracting actionable intelligence about defensive coordination patterns from tracking data.
